prompt: Stage 3-4 carousel. You are at 38 HP after five losses, level 6, holding one AD component. Your 3-cost carry is 2-star with one item; the frontline is naked. You pick first, so everything is available. Rank what you should take, from first choice to last.

steps: A completed defensive item on any unit: goes on the 2-cost tank this round
A defensive component: completes a tank item with nothing you hold, but pairs with the next drop
The AD component that completes a second carry item now
A Spatula for a future emblem

explanation:
At 38 HP every pick is judged by how much of it fights in the next combat. The completed defensive item is two components of power on a naked frontline, immediately: it is the only pick that fixes the thing killing you. Second is the AD component, because it completes a real item this round on the carry that is already your damage, even though damage is not the bigger problem. Third is the lone defensive component: it is on-theme but it is half an item until the next drop, and at five losses you may not be alive for the next drop. Last is the Spatula, which is zero power this round and a plan for a game you might not reach.

The common mistake is ranking by long-term value, which would put the Spatula and the defensive component higher. Long-term value is a stage-2 and healthy-stage-3 concept; at 38 HP the horizon is two rounds.
principle: When losing, rank carousel picks by power that fights in the next combat; everything else is a plan you may not survive to use.
commonMistake: Ranking the Spatula near the top because emblems are game-winning, on a board that has three rounds to live.
